We welcome you to the Youth Commission meeting.

If you wish to address the Commission during the meeting, please complete a speaker’s card and give it
to the secretary. The maximum time for addressing the Commission is five minutes. If you wish to
address the Commission on an item which appears on the agenda, your comments will be heard during
the Commission’s discussion of that item. If you wish to address the Commission on a subject which
does not appear on the agenda but related to recreation or community service, you may make your
presentation under agenda item VII. Please be advised that the Commission cannot, under the State of
California’s Ralph M. Brown Act, take action on any item that does not appear on the agenda.

When making your presentation, please give your name and address for the record. Please make your
statement as brief as possible. Thank you.

Minutes
  Alhambra Youth Commission
  September 9, 2025

Call to Order
The Alhambra Youth Commission was called to order at 6:01 PM on September 9, 2025, at the Alhambra Civic Center
Library, 101 South 1st Street, Alhambra, CA 91801.

I. Roll Call

Commissioners Present: Leslie Chu, Pamela Ghazale, Arabella Hernandez, Isabella Hernandez,
Katherine Quintana, Natalia Rosales, Brendon Wu.
Staff Present: Brie Houghton (Deputy Director), Rosalyn Rojas (Recreation Supervisor).
Absent: Chen Yu Wang, Lydia Chen, Siqi Li

II. Flag Salute

The Pledge of Allegiance was recited with all members standing and participating.

III. Approval of Minutes (August 12, 2025 Meeting)

Motion to approve the minutes was made by Brendon Wu and seconded by Leslie Chu. Motion passed by roll call vote.

IV. Staff Report

A. Upcoming City Events and Volunteer Opportunities
Staff reported on major city events and opportunities for Youth Commissioners to volunteer:

    Fiesta Alhambra – Latino Heritage Celebration
  o Date/Time: Sunday, September 21, 2025. Farmers Market begins at 8:00 AM; stage
  entertainment begins at 10:00 AM.
  o Location: 100 S. 2nd Street, integrated with the Farmers Market.
  o Activities: Stage with cultural performances (Aztec dancers, mariachis, conga trio), dance floor,
  vendors, kids’ zone (face painter, crafts, games), photo opportunity, and Ofrenda.
  o Volunteer Roles: Managing lines (e.g., face painter), assisting children’s games and prizes,
  supporting stage performers, and assisting with Ofrenda activities.
  o Shifts: Recommended start time 10:00–11:00 AM for peak hours; 2-hour shifts preferred. Set-up
  (from 8:00 AM) and breakdown opportunities available.
    Pumpkin Run – 5K/10K Event
  o Date/Time: Sunday, October 26, 2025.
  o Scale: Among the largest city events with extensive vendors, high attendance, and children’s
  categories.
  o Activities: Start line on Main Street, vendors, jumpers, rock climbing, balloon artists, kids’ zone
  with crafts and games, and stage entertainment.
  o Volunteer Roles: Peak-time assistance requested for managing kids’ activities, supporting
  entertainment, and line management. Setup and teardown support also needed.
  o Pre-Event Volunteer Options: Staff will confirm with external partner Joanna regarding packet
  pick-up and t-shirt distribution opportunities.
 B. Branding and Identification for Volunteers
Staff suggested designing a lanyard insert reading “Alhambra Youth Commissioner” with an engagement
tagline. Commissioners interested in graphic design may assist once sizing is provided.

C. Holiday Initiative – Spark of Love Toy Drive (Proposed)

    Partners: To be coordinated with Alhambra Fire Department (Joe Lawrence) and Parks & Recreation.
    Collection Plan: Two donation drop sites recommended (e.g., Parks & Recreation office and Library).
  Commissioners may also collect through schools, clubs, and neighborhoods, then drop off at Parks &
  Recreation.
    Communications: One commissioner will design the flyer (Natalia Rosales volunteered). Flyer to
  include Spark of Love description, drop-off locations, and Youth Commission branding.
    Social Media: Must use the City’s official accounts to comply with ADA and retention guidelines. Staff
  will adapt materials for posting.
    Timeline: Staff will confirm donation deadlines (likely early December). Final details will be presented
  at the October meeting.

D. Additional Engagement Ideas

    Commissioners discussed “Hello Neighbor,” a civic engagement initiative to connect residents with
  local community groups.
    Interest was expressed in exploring additional service projects such as food drives and toy drives, though
  timing constraints were noted.

V. Oral Communications

No additional public oral communications were presented.

VI. Commission Orals

    Several commissioners expressed interest in volunteering for both Fiesta Alhambra (Sept 21) and
  Pumpkin Run (Oct 26). Staff, Rosalyn Rojas, will coordinate volunteer shifts.
    Commissioners discussed participation in the California Association of Youth Commissions (CAYC).
  Natalia Rosales confirmed registration; at least one additional commissioner (possibly Brendon Wu) will
  also register as backup to ensure representation and continuity.
    Commissioners emphasized the importance of clear communication with staff regarding scheduling
  conflicts or cancellations.

VII. Adjournment

Staff, Brie Houghton calls the meeting to adjourn at 6:36 PM.
